body.rationale: IPS status: ratified, as given in this round's instructions, so the hard-limit breaches count. I am inverse_volatility and excluded myself. My first choice, cvar_minimization, beats my fifth, tail_risk_parity, because it has no hard IPS breach and the lowest CRO score in the compliant group (0.41). Its backtest Sharpe is 0.74 and its drawdown is -18.7%. Tail_risk_parity breaches the volatility floor (7.67% against 8%) and has a similar CRO score (0.42), so it needs a blending partner. The cvar_minimization reviewers did flag two weaknesses: only 4 of 18 assets are held, and volatility was tuned to land exactly on 8.00%. It is covariance and tail based, with no return forecast beyond a floor, which suits a late-cycle regime. Second is risk_parity: it also needs no forecast, has an effective N of 14.3, a CRO score of 0.41, a -20.3% drawdown and only a small volatility breach (7.56%). The intra-category review of maximum_diversification, a peer risk-structured method, found the weights consistent with ERC behaviour. The remaining criticisms concern the loose wording of the risk-contribution claim, not the portfolio. Third is black_litterman and fourth is resampled_efficient_frontier. Both clear every hard limit. Black_litterman has a -21.9% drawdown but a questionable AUM-based prior, noted in the max_sharpe review. Resampled_efficient_frontier is better diversified (13.1) but its -24.84% drawdown is only 16bp inside the limit, so it is fragile. Fifth is tail_risk_parity, which adds the non-traditional family and a downside-covariance view, though the intra-category review noted that semicovariance is not a true tail measure. I flag market_cap_weight: the CRO score is 0.80 and the backtest drawdown is -40.6%, 15.6 points past the limit. About 77% is equity beta. Two reviewers noted that ETF AUM weights are not the market portfolio and double-count overlapping style funds. The proposal itself calls the portfolio a diagnostic, not a recommendation, so the CIO should not lean on it. I did not flag adversarial_diversifier, which has value as an orthogonal ensemble member even though it breaches return, volatility and tracking error as a standalone portfolio.
